correctness.rationale: For every p>=3 with N=2p, full Gaussian window variance 1/(2p), even modulations and translations 0,1, character orthogonality decomposes S=GG* into p two-dimensional blocks. The p=0 seam swaps the two Gaussian half-coordinates; with V_a=sqrt(2p)*(g_a,g_{a+p}) and independent standard complex Gaussians, B_a=0.5(V_a V_a*+W_a W_a*), det B_a=|det[V_a,W_a]|^2/4. Thus H=-p log 4+2 sum log R_a+sum log D_a with R_a~Gamma(shape2,scale1), D_a~Uniform(0,1). Adjacent angular D logs are uncorrelated by conditioning on the shared Haar direction (not jointly independent around the cycle), all radii are independent, hence E H=p(1-2 EulerGamma-log4), Var H=p(2 pi^2/3-3). Nonseam logdet terms form a stationary one-dependent sequence with finite moments; the single seam contributes o_P(sqrt(p)), proving the CLT, and Chebyshev yields the geometric-mean law. Independent full-matrix/block determinant reconstruction checked 75 random instances p=3,4,6; finite tests are only corroboration.
residual_risks: Finite checks are corroborations only; analytic proof establishes universal parameters.

evidence: Deterministic block equivalence alone does not force the law of products under correlated Gaussian blocks. The phase-only independent-fiber law has singular support at fixed amplitude and cannot be substituted into the Gaussian theorem. The hard-edge Poisson law does not determine a sum of logarithms. The missing step is exactly the Gamma/Haar decomposition, pairwise angular covariance cancellation and one-dependent CLT.

originality.rationale: Published Asipchuk–De Carli–Rodriguez give subgroup block equivalence but no Gaussian exact logdet moments or growing-p CLT in the inspected relevant text. A same-geometry Gaussian paper gives a Poisson law for the *least eigenvalue*, not log volume; its shared block factorization is credited. A phase-only window theorem has a logdet CLT but uses constant-amplitude independent phases and different exact constants. Its distributional law does not imply the Gaussian amplitude/radius covariance contribution. Best-of-knowledge surviving novelty is these precise Gaussian moments and one-dependent CLT.
residual_risks: A more general published log-volume limit for complex Gaussian one-dependent random Gram blocks might imply the same special case under another title.
The source block-equivalence framework is prior; only stochastic exact constants and CLT are credited.

value.rationale: Log-volume is a natural independent conditioning/entropy statistic of a critical random Gabor basis, distinct from extremal frame bounds. The proof correctly accounts for coordinate reuse, finds exact finite-size mean and variance for all p, and identifies a nontrivial 1-dependent Gaussian limit. The seam twist and radial covariance make it more than simply treating blocks as independent Wishart matrices.
